versions.summary: The first release of webOS Phoenix: the cards, gestures and Just Type of classic webOS, with new apps, Synergy and a Marketplace.
new: Every app runs in its own card: cards stack by task, a flick up closes one, and dragging one off the bottom forces it closed.
The gesture area: swipe up for card view and the launcher, swipe back to go back, and hold it to talk to the Assistant.
Just Type: start typing anywhere to find apps, contacts, messages and the web, or to start an email, a message or a memo.
Notifications as webOS showed them: banners, the notification bar and dashboards, with an app's notifications of one kind stacked in one dashboard.
The launcher with its tabs and the quick launch bar, and press and hold on an icon for its options.
The lock screen, the status bar and the system menu of webOS, on phones and on tablets.
Synergy: contacts and calendars from CardDAV and CalDAV servers, email, and chats from Jabber, Matrix, Delta Chat, Telegram and the Fediverse, each in one place.
The Marketplace: popular web apps, apps packaged for Phoenix and open-source web apps, from signed catalogs, with updates.
Classics in the Marketplace: the original webOS apps of the App Museum II and the Preware feeds, when you switch them on.
The Assistant answers what you ask by voice or by typing, aloud if you like, on the device itself.
Say “Hey Phoenix” to ask the Assistant hands-free, once you switch it on in Settings.
The webOS keyboards, with dictation, word suggestions, swipe typing, emoji and cursor control.
New apps: Settings, Phone, Messaging, Camera, Photos, Music, Files, Tasks, Voice Memos, Weather, Maps, Passwords, Terminal and more.
The original Open webOS apps run as they were: Calendar, Contacts, Email, Memos, Calculator, Clock and Accounts.
Share from any app's menu with the share sheet, and paste from the clipboard history.
System updates install next to the running system while you use your device, and it goes back if the new one does not start.
Settings finds drivers and firmware for your device's hardware in a signed catalog.
Developer Mode, found by typing the Konami code in Just Type, as on webOS.
A start-up animation of a phoenix that burns to ash and rises again, or the classic glowing logo.
Sharp art and text on every screen, from the Pre's to today's.
known: Phoenix runs in the simulator; its images for phones and tablets are written but not yet tried on a device.
Calls and texts use simulated telephony until Phoenix runs on a device with a modem.
Mojo apps from the App Museum do not run: the Mojo framework was never released as open source.
Pinyin and handwriting input are not there yet.
